text:
maya-support: FYI AcmeCorp is hitting persistent 429s + tail latency on their Dedicated pool (quiet-west-2). Started ~09:12 UTC after a plan sync. Customer says traffic is within their usual range. Screenshots + request ids attached.
ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-429-rate-high quiet-west-2 — 430 429s/min. https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/ALERT-7g2b
kevin-acme: hey, thanks for the flag. tenant_id=t-acme-42. sample request_id=01FZ9X2K7. curl below shows 429: 
```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 3 }
```
maya-support: timestamped logs show surge at 09:12 but sustained 429s after. Not a typical burst.
sam-oncall: can someone check per-tenant quota mapping and whether burst allowances are being applied for dedicated pools?
jordan-eng: running quick query against quota-service now: `SELECT tenant_id, plan_tag, qps, burst_tokens FROM tenant_quotas WHERE tenant_id='t-acme-42'`
lena-sre: ping when you have results — also check scheduler logs for warmup/backoff. quietpool scheduler has been flaky after last deploy.
jordan-eng: result: `t-acme-42 | plan_tag=enterprise-dedicated | qps=100 | burst_tokens=0` — burst_tokens=0 looks wrong for that plan. plan config should provide burst_tokens=600.
kevin-acme: we definitely had burst on previous weeks. plan sync happened ~09:10 per billing webhook.
maya-support: that explains sustained 429s even though qps looks okay in short windows. If burst_tokens is zero, long-running usage will hit the ceiling.
jordan-eng: digging into plan-sync worker logs: it processed plan change events out of order. I see a race where `apply_plan_to_tenant` runs before `materialize_burst_profile`. The handler set plan_tag but didn't seed burst cache. stack trace shows `KeyError: 'burst_profile'` swallowed and we continued.
lena-sre: ugh — error handler suppressed the failure. scheduler then marked tenant as "no-burst" which pins them to steady qps only.
sam-oncall: mitigation options? can we temporarily set a per-tenant override?
jordan-eng: yes — admin command: `rbac set-quota t-acme-42 --qps 100 --burst 600 --reason "temp override after plan-sync race"` — running now.
ops-bot: ACTION: quota-override applied by jordan-eng. ticket #SR-5421.
kevin-acme: after override our requests are accepted again, latency improved within 2 minutes. thank you. :relieved:
maya-support: great. customer confirms recovery. marking incident resolved for customer-facing part.
jordan-eng: root cause: plan-sync ordering race + swallowed exception in materialize step. Proposed permanent fix: (1) make materialize_burst_profile transactional with apply_plan, (2) add alert when burst_tokens==0 for dedicated plans, (3) add unit test for plan-sync ordering.
lena-sre: also add a post-deploy smoke check for quota seeding on reserved pools.
sam-oncall: I'll own the rollback/patch timeline. ETA for hotfix is 3h, postmortem afterwards.
maya-support: notes for support playbook: if customer on dedicated reports sustained 429s after plan change, check `burst_tokens` in tenant_quotas and apply override as temporary fix.
kevin-acme: appreciate the quick help team. please keep me updated on the permanent fix.
jordan-eng: will follow up in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
